name: Voice AI interview study

picks.name: Definitional analysis
picks.reason: Terms such as satisfying, abandon and disclosed need fixed working definitions before any transcript can be judged for or against a hypothesis.
picks.purpose: Replaces ambiguous key terms with precise working definitions and produces a glossary with borderline cases.

picks.name: Hypothesis tree
picks.reason: Splitting each of the seven hypotheses into the sub-claims that must hold shows exactly which evidence each one needs.
picks.purpose: Splits a claim into the sub-claims that must all be true for it to be true and produces a tree of claims that goes into a claims register.

picks.name: Quality of information check
picks.reason: All eight transcripts come from one source with narrative depth only, so this check shows which findings rest on a single voice and how much of the picture is missing.
picks.purpose: Rates the completeness, accuracy and corroboration of each source and produces a source database with a statement of what is known and unknown.

picks.name: Framework analysis
picks.reason: A transcript by hypothesis matrix with an audit trail gives a visible base for reading across the eight interviews and spotting where they disagree.
picks.purpose: Sorts coded qualitative data into a case by theme matrix and produces the matrix for reading across cases and themes.

picks.name: Source-span and quotation check by code
picks.reason: Any quotation or coded statement drawn from a transcript, especially if a model helps with coding, must be confirmed by string match to exist in the source.
picks.purpose: Require each extracted statement to point to the exact passage it came from, confirm by string match that the passage exists, and produce a pass or fail list per statement.

picks.name: Comparative case study
picks.reason: Treating each transcript as a case with the same questions reaches the associate level and shows consistent patterns and deviant cases for each hypothesis.
picks.purpose: Examines a small number of cases with the same questions for each, producing a case by case matrix that shows consistent patterns and deviant cases.

picks.name: Absence analysis
picks.reason: Several hypotheses may simply not be addressed in the interviews, and this separates silence from evidence against.
picks.purpose: Draws a conclusion from an item missing from a document or comparison set where it would be expected if a claim were true, producing a list of expected but absent items.

picks.name: Analysis of competing hypotheses
picks.reason: Rating each evidence item against rival readings of each hypothesis shows which evidence discriminates and which only fits everything, and it reaches the associate level.
picks.purpose: Lists plausible hypotheses, rates each evidence item against each, and produces a hypothesis by evidence matrix aimed at disproving hypotheses.

picks.name: Disconfirmation search
picks.reason: A deliberate search for contradicting statements in the transcripts tests each apparently supported hypothesis, such as the satisfaction and abandonment claims.
picks.purpose: Looks for evidence that would contradict a favoured claim and produces a list of refuting evidence found or not found with the search used.

picks.name: Sensitivity analysis
picks.reason: Re-running the verdicts after dropping single transcripts or changing definitions shows whether a conclusion from only eight interviews reverses.
picks.purpose: Re-runs an analysis under different assumptions or inclusion rules and produces a table of results by assumption showing whether the conclusion reverses.

picks.name: Cognitive bias checks and debiasing
picks.reason: A bias check guards against confirmation of the stated hypotheses and over-weighting of vivid interviews before a decision-informing result is released.
picks.purpose: Runs a conclusion through a list of known judgement biases, applies a counter-procedure, and produces a checklist of marked items where disconfirming evidence should be sought.

picks.name: Independent human review of model output
picks.reason: A second person who did not build the analysis should review the verdicts and be able to overrule them, which suits a decision-informing job with personal information in the transcripts.
picks.purpose: Specify who reviews which outputs, with what rubric and with authority to overrule, and produce a review log with decisions.

gaps: No listed technique supplies a statistical test of association, which eight narrative interviews could not support anyway, so the associate claim must be stated as patterns within this sample only. None addresses a baseline for traditional automation unless the transcripts themselves compare the two, and none covers de-identification or privacy handling of personal information in the transcripts.

name: Diagnose low AI adoption

picks.name: Data profiling and rule-based validation
picks.reason: The usage analytics and survey tables need profiling for completeness, validity and consistency before any figure is read.
picks.purpose: Describe the structure, completeness, validity and consistency of each field and test explicit rules, giving a profile table per column and a list of records that break each rule.

picks.name: Hypothesis tree
picks.reason: Splits each of the eight master hypotheses into sub-claims that must hold, so the evidence can be pointed at testable statements.
picks.purpose: Splits a claim into the sub-claims that must all be true for it to be true and produces a tree of claims that goes into a claims register.

picks.name: Key assumptions check
picks.reason: Surfaces the unstated premises behind the eight barriers, such as low usage meaning low adoption, and records what would show each false.
picks.purpose: Lists the stated and unstated premises of the current line, challenges each, and produces a refined assumptions register with the conditions that would invalidate each assumption.

picks.name: Exploratory data analysis with plots and distribution checks
picks.reason: Plots usage and survey distributions, outliers and subgroup differences to see the adoption pattern before explaining it.
picks.purpose: Examine a cleaned table with plots and summary statistics to find shape, outliers, trends, subgroup differences and broken assumptions, and produce a draft result of plots and summaries.

picks.name: Subgroup and Simpson's paradox check
picks.reason: Checks whether pooled adoption patterns reverse or vanish within teams, roles or personas of unequal size, which would mislead the barrier diagnosis.
picks.purpose: Recomputes an association within subgroups to see whether the pooled direction reverses or vanishes and produces pooled and stratified estimates side by side.

picks.name: Framework analysis
picks.reason: Sorts coded interview content into a case by hypothesis matrix with an audit trail, suiting interview evidence with no shared identifier to the tables.
picks.purpose: Sorts coded qualitative data into a case by theme matrix and produces the matrix for reading across cases and themes.

picks.name: Convergent comparison of qualitative and quantitative results
picks.reason: Analyses interview, usage and survey strands separately then merges them by topic, which works without a record level link between sources.
picks.purpose: Analyses qualitative and quantitative results on the same topic separately, then merges them to compare and produces a comparison of agreement, partial agreement and discordance by topic.

picks.name: Joint display
picks.reason: Shows what the numbers and the narrative say about each barrier in one matrix so agreement and conflict are visible to decision makers.
picks.purpose: Places quantitative and qualitative results in one table, figure or matrix with shared row labels and produces a matrix that shows where the strands agree, expand each other or conflict.

picks.name: Analysis of competing hypotheses
picks.reason: Rates every evidence item against all eight hypotheses to find which evidence discriminates and which barriers can be set aside.
picks.purpose: Lists plausible hypotheses, rates each evidence item against each, and produces a hypothesis by evidence matrix aimed at disproving hypotheses.

picks.name: Realist evaluation
picks.reason: Frames each surviving barrier as a context, mechanism and outcome configuration, which directly answers by what mechanism and for whom.
picks.purpose: Tests what works for whom and in what circumstances through context, mechanism and outcome configurations and produces a refined program theory.

picks.name: Process tracing
picks.reason: Applies diagnostic tests to rival explanations within this single organisation, reaching the mechanism level needed.
picks.purpose: Tests what each rival hypothesis predicts against diagnostic evidence within one case and produces a test result per hypothesis in a hypotheses matrix.

picks.name: Counterfactual analysis
picks.reason: Argues what adoption would look like if a given barrier were removed, supplying the counterfactual the decision needs where no comparison group exists.
picks.purpose: Sets the actual outcome against an argued account of what would have happened had one factor differed and produces a counterfactual scenario.

picks.name: Disconfirmation search
picks.reason: Searches the three evidence sources for material that contradicts the favoured explanation before it is relied on.
picks.purpose: Looks for evidence that would contradict a favoured claim and produces a list of refuting evidence found or not found with the search used.

picks.name: Sensitivity analysis
picks.reason: Re-runs the conclusions under different coding, inclusion and survey handling choices to show whether the barrier ranking holds.
picks.purpose: Re-runs an analysis under different assumptions or inclusion rules and produces a table of results by assumption showing whether the conclusion reverses.

gaps: No listed technique supports a controlled estimate of how much adoption would rise if a barrier were removed, because no comparison group or pre and post data are described; the counterfactual rests on argued reasoning only. Nothing listed handles privacy controls for personal information in interview and analytics records, and no technique links staff across sources without an identifier, so findings stay at topic or group level.

name: Explain results against targets

picks.name: Data profiling and rule-based validation
picks.reason: Profiles the usage records by user and shift for completeness, validity and duplicates before any figure is explained, and checks the shared identifier that links usage to interviewees.
picks.purpose: Describe the structure, completeness, validity and consistency of each field and test explicit rules, giving a profile table per column and a list of records that break each rule.

picks.name: Distribution, outlier and base-rate checks
picks.reason: Checks the shape, outliers and base rates behind the 72% and 45% figures so that a few heavy or absent users are not mistaken for a shift effect.
picks.purpose: Examines the shape, extremes and baseline frequency of data before a figure is interpreted and produces histograms, summary statistics, flagged outliers and a base rate.

picks.name: Gap analysis
picks.reason: Sets out the gap between actual and target for usage and time reduction so that the shortfall to be explained is stated precisely.
picks.purpose: Compares current with desired performance, producing a prioritised list of gaps and the means to close each.

picks.name: Exploratory data analysis with plots and distribution checks
picks.reason: Plots usage by shift, user and any other available field to see how the gap is distributed and what else varies with shift.
picks.purpose: Examine a cleaned table with plots and summary statistics to find shape, outliers, trends, subgroup differences and broken assumptions, and produce a draft result of plots and summaries.

picks.name: Subgroup and Simpson's paradox check
picks.reason: Recomputes the usage gap within strata to test whether the morning and afternoon difference is a composition effect, such as different roles or users, and not a shift effect.
picks.purpose: Recomputes an association within subgroups to see whether the pooled direction reverses or vanishes and produces pooled and stratified estimates side by side.

picks.name: Hypothesis tree
picks.reason: Splits 'why results fell short' into sub-claims that can each be tested, such as lower afternoon usage, weaker time savings per use, and target setting.
picks.purpose: Splits a claim into the sub-claims that must all be true for it to be true and produces a tree of claims that goes into a claims register.

picks.name: Framework analysis
picks.reason: Codes the staff interviews into a case by theme matrix that can be read by shift, giving the qualitative side an audit trail.
picks.purpose: Sorts coded qualitative data into a case by theme matrix and produces the matrix for reading across cases and themes.

picks.name: Explanatory sequential integration
picks.reason: Uses the quantitative pattern of 85% against 45% to choose which interview material to read for an explanation, which suits the surprising shift gap.
picks.purpose: Uses a completed quantitative result, especially an unexpected or extreme one, to choose the qualitative material read to explain it and produces an explanation linked to the numeric pattern.

picks.name: Joint display
picks.reason: Places usage figures and interview themes in one matrix by shift so that agreement and conflict between the two evidence strands are visible.
picks.purpose: Places quantitative and qualitative results in one table, figure or matrix with shared row labels and produces a matrix that shows where the strands agree, expand each other or conflict.

picks.name: Analysis of competing hypotheses
picks.reason: Rates each piece of evidence against rival explanations for the afternoon gap, such as staffing, workload, supervision and tool fit, to find which evidence discriminates.
picks.purpose: Lists plausible hypotheses, rates each evidence item against each, and produces a hypothesis by evidence matrix aimed at disproving hypotheses.

picks.name: Realist evaluation
picks.reason: Frames findings as context, mechanism and outcome configurations, which reaches the mechanism claim level by explaining why the initiative works in the morning context and not the afternoon one.
picks.purpose: Tests what works for whom and in what circumstances through context, mechanism and outcome configurations and produces a refined program theory.

picks.name: Counterfactual analysis
picks.reason: Argues what usage and time reduction would have been had afternoon conditions matched morning ones, giving the counterfactual claim the question asks for.
picks.purpose: Sets the actual outcome against an argued account of what would have happened had one factor differed and produces a counterfactual scenario.

picks.name: Disconfirmation search
picks.reason: Searches for evidence that contradicts the favoured mechanism before it informs a decision.
picks.purpose: Looks for evidence that would contradict a favoured claim and produces a list of refuting evidence found or not found with the search used.

gaps: No listed technique covers privacy handling or de-identification of personal information in record-level data and interviews. The evidence has no data on staffing, workload, tools or supervision by shift, and no comparison group or before and after data, so mechanism claims will rest on interview evidence and argued counterfactuals and not on estimated effects. The time reduction shortfall has no shift breakdown in the stated evidence.

purposes.CM1-15: Compares current with desired performance, producing a prioritised list of gaps and the means to close each.
purposes.TC1-05: Sets the actual outcome against an argued account of what would have happened had one factor differed and produces a counterfactual scenario.
purposes.TC1-11: Tests what works for whom and in what circumstances through context, mechanism and outcome configurations and produces a refined program theory.
purposes.DM-02: Splits a claim into the sub-claims that must all be true for it to be true and produces a tree of claims that goes into a claims register.
purposes.TC-05: Recomputes an association within subgroups to see whether the pooled direction reverses or vanishes and produces pooled and stratified estimates side by side.
purposes.MM-01: Examine a cleaned table with plots and summary statistics to find shape, outliers, trends, subgroup differences and broken assumptions, and produce a draft result of plots and summaries.
purposes.IS-08: Places quantitative and qualitative results in one table, figure or matrix with shared row labels and produces a matrix that shows where the strands agree, expand each other or conflict.
purposes.TC1-16: Looks for evidence that would contradict a favoured claim and produces a list of refuting evidence found or not found with the search used.

name: Synthesise research reports

picks.name: Document and policy analysis
picks.reason: Extracts each report's claims, positions and stated reasons into one table using its provenance and purpose, which is the base for every later comparison.
picks.purpose: Reads documents systematically to extract facts, positions, changes or stated reasons using their provenance and purpose, and produces an extraction table or chronology.

picks.name: Source-span and quotation check by code
picks.reason: Confirms by string match that each extracted statement and quotation exists in its report, so the synthesis does not rest on misread or invented passages.
picks.purpose: Require each extracted statement to point to the exact passage it came from, confirm by string match that the passage exists, and produce a pass or fail list per statement.

picks.name: Grey literature appraisal checklist
picks.reason: Scores each report on authority, accuracy, coverage, objectivity, date and significance, which suits the mix of academic, vendor and consultancy producers.
picks.purpose: Scores a non-peer-reviewed item on six criteria (authority, accuracy, coverage, objectivity, date, significance) and produces a completed checklist.

picks.name: Source dependence and copy detection
picks.reason: Tests whether the reports draw on a shared upstream source, since the Meeker report and others may reuse Stanford HAI data and so agreement would not be independent.
picks.purpose: Estimates whether sources copy from each other so that their agreement is not counted as independent support and produces a dependence estimate for source pairs or groups.

picks.name: Admiralty system
picks.reason: Grades each report for source reliability and information credibility, giving a direct answer to how far each can be trusted.
picks.purpose: Assigns each report a two-character grade for source reliability (A to F) and information credibility (1 to 6) and produces an appraised evidence base.

picks.name: Quality of information check
picks.reason: Shows which findings rest on a single source and what is unknown, so weakly corroborated claims are marked in the position.
picks.purpose: Rates the completeness, accuracy and corroboration of each source and produces a source database with a statement of what is known and unknown.

picks.name: Lens application
picks.reason: Sorts claims by kind (measured result, forecast, case anecdote, opinion) so that agreement is compared like for like and missing evidence types are visible.
picks.purpose: Sorts a set of claims or measures by chosen categories, such as input or outcome, and produces a table of claims by category.

picks.name: Claim and citation verification against source text
picks.reason: Checks whether claims that cite other studies or data are backed by those sources, which helps separate vendor assertion from supported finding.
picks.purpose: Labels each claim as supported, refuted or not enough information against retrieved evidence, or rates whether a cited source supports its claim, and produces a label with evidence sentences.

picks.name: Triangulation
picks.reason: Builds the convergence table of agreement, disagreement and reasons across the five reports, which answers the agree and conflict parts of the question.
picks.purpose: Compares independent lines of evidence on one question and produces a convergence table of agreement, disagreement and reasons.

picks.name: Rapoport's rules
picks.reason: Restates each conflicting position fairly and lists points of agreement before rebuttal, so real disagreements are separated from differences in framing or scope.
picks.purpose: Requires a fair restatement of the opposing position, a list of points of agreement and of what was learned before any rebuttal, and produces a restatement and an agreement list.

picks.name: Absence analysis
picks.reason: Lists topics and evidence a report would be expected to include but omits, such as costs, failures or frontline staff outcomes, which bears on both trust and conflict.
picks.purpose: Draws a conclusion from an item missing from a document or comparison set where it would be expected if a claim were true, producing a list of expected but absent items.

picks.name: Disconfirmation search
picks.reason: Searches for credible evidence against the emerging consensus on AI adoption in customer-facing teams before the position is relied on.
picks.purpose: Looks for evidence that would contradict a favoured claim and produces a list of refuting evidence found or not found with the search used.

picks.name: Narrative, thematic and qualitative evidence synthesis
picks.reason: Combines the findings in words and themes linked back to each report, since the reports cannot be pooled numerically and the output is the single position needed.
picks.purpose: Combines findings across studies in words or themes when pooling numbers is not appropriate, and produces a structured narrative or theme set linked back to studies.

picks.name: Key assumptions check
picks.reason: Records the assumptions the combined position depends on and the conditions that would show them false, as a final check for a decision-informing use.
picks.purpose: Lists the stated and unstated premises of the current line, challenges each, and produces a refined assumptions register with the conditions that would invalidate each assumption.

gaps: No listed technique suits a test of sponsor effects across only five reports (CM-01 reaches associate level and needs many reports). There is also no technique built for appraising a single experimental paper such as the Cybernetic Teammate study beyond the generic design checklist HE-02, which I left out. Reports restricted by copyright limit how much text can be quoted in outputs. Otherwise none; the describe level is reached by the chosen techniques.

name: Prioritise AI initiatives

picks.name: Decision-first framing
picks.reason: Starts from the funding decision and the options it could change, so only questions that affect which initiative is funded first are asked.
picks.purpose: Starts from the decision to be made and works back to a list of questions, each tagged with the option it could change.

picks.name: Definitional analysis
picks.reason: Fixes working definitions of the four scored dimensions and of what a score means, so the scores can be compared and the ranking is not an artefact of wording.
picks.purpose: Replaces ambiguous key terms with precise working definitions and produces a glossary with borderline cases.

picks.name: Data profiling and rule-based validation
picks.reason: Profiles the score table for completeness, valid ranges and consistency before any ranking is computed.
picks.purpose: Describe the structure, completeness, validity and consistency of each field and test explicit rules, giving a profile table per column and a list of records that break each rule.

picks.name: Missing data diagnosis and treatment
picks.reason: Diagnoses and treats any initiatives with missing scores so that gaps do not silently shift a rank.
picks.purpose: Measure how much is missing, where and for whom, then choose deletion, imputation or weighting, giving the missing share by field and subgroup and a cleaned dataset.

picks.name: Distribution, outlier and base-rate checks
picks.reason: Checks the spread and extremes of each score so that a single outlier or a compressed scale does not drive the ranking.
picks.purpose: Examines the shape, extremes and baseline frequency of data before a figure is interpreted and produces histograms, summary statistics, flagged outliers and a base rate.

picks.name: Key assumptions check
picks.reason: Lists the premises behind the scores and the ranking, such as scale comparability and independence of initiatives, with the conditions that would invalidate each.
picks.purpose: Lists the stated and unstated premises of the current line, challenges each, and produces a refined assumptions register with the conditions that would invalidate each assumption.

picks.name: Group process safeguards
picks.reason: Records independent views on criterion weights before discussion, because weights are a judgement that a senior voice could otherwise set.
picks.purpose: Controls how a group forms views, with each person contributing in turn, leaders withholding early preferences and evaluators rotating, and produces independent individual views.

picks.name: Structured expert elicitation
picks.reason: Elicits ranges for the weights and for score uncertainty from a small panel, giving the inputs needed to say how sure the ranking is.
picks.purpose: Elicit numeric estimates and ranges from experts before and after discussion and aggregate them mathematically, giving aggregated estimates with intervals as a draft result.

picks.name: Multi-criteria decision analysis
picks.reason: Combines the four criteria into weighted scores and a ranking, which is the direct answer to which initiative should be funded first.
picks.purpose: Scores options against several weighted criteria, producing weights, scores and a ranking, with a test of how the ranking changes when weights change.

picks.name: Agent-based modelling and Monte Carlo simulation
picks.reason: Draws weights and scores from their uncertainty ranges many times to give rank distributions, the only listed route to a forward-looking statement of confidence that does not imply cause.
picks.purpose: Simulate agents or random draws many times to give an outcome distribution with tail probabilities and the inputs that account for the spread, as a draft result.

picks.name: Sensitivity analysis
picks.reason: Re-runs the ranking under alternative weights, scoring rules and inclusion choices to show whether the top choice reverses.
picks.purpose: Re-runs an analysis under different assumptions or inclusion rules and produces a table of results by assumption showing whether the conclusion reverses.

picks.name: Two by two matrix
picks.reason: Plots value against risk in a quadrant view that lets decision makers see trade-offs the single ranking hides.
picks.purpose: Places items on two chosen dimensions so that each falls into one of four cells and produces a quadrant table.

picks.name: Scripted reproducible workflow
picks.reason: Records data, weights and code so that the ranking and its uncertainty can be regenerated and audited by someone else.
picks.purpose: Record data, code and environment so that another person or a later run can regenerate every figure, and produce a project record that can be rerun from the raw data.

gaps: No listed technique takes a human-reviewed check of the final recommendation as a decision-informing control beyond CK-26, which targets model output and was not selected. No technique is specific to ranking stability metrics such as rank correlation or top-k membership frequency, so these would be built within the Monte Carlo step. Otherwise none.
